name: Bhavika Agarwal
feedback: The label explanation and four-step preference flow make the intended benefit understandable. The app still feels like a first pass: Save to Log showed no confirmation, Saved points to the demo analysis, and completing onboarding then refreshing returned to step one; complete a persistent scan-to-saved-result loop.
tested: Home, demo analysis, Scan, Saved route, all four onboarding steps
Save to Log click; Get Started then refresh reset onboarding
limitations: Camera and gallery upload not used; actual recognition unverified
Desktop content occupied a small corner of viewport

name: Shivanand Shukla
feedback: The campus feed, search and leaderboard form a clear, visually coherent social app, and an unmatched search correctly shows an empty state. I expected a clearer demo boundary and a verifiable posting-to-profile loop; the review stopped before sending any AMA or message.
tested: Home, Search, Community, My Profile and AMA composer
limitations: No communications sent; posting, messaging and persistence of those actions unverified

name: Mansha Bhardwaj
feedback: The film theme is consistent, and setup, movie reveal, hints and team scoring create a playable loop. I expected an in-progress game to survive refresh; refreshing returned to the start screen, so add a saved-game/resume path.
tested: Setup 30s, revealed Chennai Express, hint then Got It
limitations: Full three-round finish not exercised

name: Deveshwar Singh Chhinna
feedback: This is a thoughtful simulation: improving product changed quality, cash and runway, month advancement persisted after refresh, and the coach used those exact figures in its response. The navigation includes clear empty states for meetings and term sheets; I expected the remaining pitch-to-negotiation journey to be equally testable, with model assumptions explained.
tested: Improve Product, End month, refresh retained month 2
AI Coach returned contextual guidance with ₹41L cash and quality 31
limitations: Full investor pitch and negotiation cycle not completed

name: Vaishnavi Nanda
feedback: Rooted has a calm, distinctive visual language and a broad relationship-care journey. The onboarding names carried into Settings, but the added bucket-list dream was absent after refresh and the dashboard showed a fixed 127-day relationship without a start date; I expected saved user data and consistent empty states instead of seeded history.
tested: Onboarding with synthetic names; Home, Garden, Bucket List, Little Things, Us, Settings, Repair
Added Test picnic and refreshed; item absent
limitations: No notes sent; drawing and shared partner synchronization untested

name: Shristy Jain
feedback: The login screen is clean and easy to read. I could not inspect repair selection or booking because the entry requires a phone number and agreement to terms; provide a guest demo or test access so the core journey can be assessed.
tested: Viewed phone-login screen and available sign-up entry
limitations: No phone entered, terms not accepted; unseen screens unknown

name: Priya Ramesh Dolas
feedback: The submitted link shows “No Lovable project found at this address,” and the supplied Drive brief was unavailable to the review connection. Please republish the project and supply a working public URL so the actual app can be assessed.
tested: Supplied Drive brief returned404 to connector

Brief also unavailable to review connection

name: Ritoban Das
feedback: The WealthQuest entry screen has a polished visual identity and a clear financial-goal proposition. Sign-in blocks the actual planning journey, so I expected demo access or test credentials before assessing the calculations, goal updates and persistence.
limitations: Authenticated app unseen; no account created

name: Shourya Mehta
feedback: The habit-to-game reward loop is well connected: completing hydration added 50 XP and a session, playing Odd or Even consumed one session and awarded 35 XP, and both persisted after refresh. I expected clearer separation of the seeded streak/history from new-user activity, and more informative feedback than “Nice intuition” on an incorrect guess.
tested: Completed hydration; Odd prediction, picked 3, CPU 1, total 4 result
Refresh retained 265 XP, two sessions and completed habit
limitations: Other two minigames not completed

name: Anish Potla
feedback: The arcade presentation is consistent, and losing produced a discovery ticket that remained in the archive after refresh. The game-to-discovery loop is thoughtfully connected; I expected clearer provenance and dates on recommendations plus a more accessible way to understand game state outside the visual playfield.
tested: Started game; lost with score 2 and received TECH NEWS ticket
Opened archive and verified same ticket after refresh
limitations: Did not open external news links; movement controls not exhaustively tested

name: Ashwini Shreedharan Pillai
feedback: The secret-clue handoff is thoughtfully implemented: four named players unlocked individual clues, followed by a live timer and an explained reveal. I expected the game to collect a team accusation before showing the solution; End Game Now jumps directly to the Butler reveal, so add an answer-and-feedback step.
tested: Case selection, four-player setup, four triple-tap clue reveals
Started timer, End Game Now, solution, refresh and instructions
limitations: One case completed; other cases not exhaustively checked

name: Karmanye Madan
feedback: The visual style is tidy and the identity-selection prompt is clear. Selecting Student led to a prefilled “The Athlete” profile, while Journey, Habits and Insights all returned to the same identity page; this feels like a first pass that needs distinct screens and an actual habit-creation/check-in loop.
tested: Selected Student, continued to Athlete profile
Tested all main navigation destinations; refreshed identity screen
limitations: No functioning habit creation or progress update found

name: PRAGYA RATHI
feedback: The analyst workspace is visually organized and offers useful transcript, peer and KPI views. Its data continuity needs substantial work: TCS analysis led to a report about “Project Quantum” with a dollar price target, and fiscal periods differ across screens; I expected one selected company and period to drive every result with traceable source evidence.
tested: Applied Wipro filter and inspected output
limitations: Own transcript upload not tested; financial figures not independently audited

name: Saanvi Jindal
feedback: The case dossier and choice-to-debrief experience are engaging, with a useful explanation after choosing the Maggi strategy. Progress is inconsistent: Intel showed one evaluated dossier and 100% accuracy while its case log still marked Maggi unsolved; I expected consistent completion tracking and direct evidence links rather than source homepages.
tested: Made Maggi Option A decision and viewed historical debrief
limitations: AI generation not submitted; linked historical claims not independently verified

name: Yashika Singh
feedback: Union Swap presents the skill-exchange proposition clearly in a coherent entry screen. The browse link redirects to a college-email account gate, so I could not test matching or exchanges; provide guest access or a test account to make the core workflow reviewable.
limitations: Authenticated features unknown; no account created

name: Taruni Gupta
feedback: Recess has a clear game catalogue and a welcoming, signup-free nickname-to-game flow; Book Cricket reached a playable page-flip screen. I expected a resume option after refresh, which returned to player setup, and clearer labeling of the fixed Active Friends sidebar within a same-device play experience.
tested: Page flip clicked; refresh returned to player setup with nickname kept
limitations: Book Cricket finish and other eight games not exhaustively tested

name: Arpita Deshpande
feedback: Clario is a well-structured domain prototype with clear risk prioritization and honest fictional-data/legal limitations. Completing a task updated its status and counts, but refresh restored the original open state; I expected persistent action tracking and reconciliation of the −6% headline with the −14% milestone gap shown below it.
tested: Portfolio, Tasks, Risk Radar, Calendar, Documents, Finance, Progress
Completed first task: Completed count 1; refresh reverted to 0
limitations: Copilot responses and external document ingestion not fully tested

name: Rishabh Kamath
feedback: The large controls and calm visual treatment suit the intended elder-care audience, and medication/history/care screens are easy to find. The non-prescription add flow jumped straight to schedule selection without asking which medicine, so I expected complete medicine identity and dosage capture before saving; refills, SOS and caregiver notifications remain unverified.
tested: Home, Meds Current Dose/History, Care, Add Medicine non-prescription route
limitations: No dose confirmations, medication saves, SOS, calls, purchases or personal health inputs submitted

name: Ayush Garg
feedback: The road-crossing theme is distinctive and the game responds to keyboard movement, score changes and a clear pause menu. I expected progress to be reflected consistently: after crossing one road the menu screens still showed zero achievements and personal best, so explain whether runs must finish before these update and preserve unfinished progress.
tested: How to Play; started game, ArrowUp yielded 10 points/one road; Pause
limitations: Run exited through Main menu before game over; final-run persistence not established

name: Muskaan Khandpur
feedback: The landing page explains the audit scope and free offer clearly, and the sign-in screen is visually consistent. Start Free Audit leads to authentication, so audit generation, scoring and saved plans could not be assessed; include a public sample or guest workflow.
tested: Landing page and Start Free Audit to sign-in
limitations: Audit screens unknown; no account created

name: Yoshita Bajaj
feedback: Yaar has a strong voice and coherent food-discovery screens; choosing South Indian reduced eight budget matches to two appropriate dishes. I expected a clear demo boundary and review-before-payment: Squad and Lucky Guess promise immediate UPI/wallet debit, while the seeded profile claims linked search and social history; those transactions and integrations were not exercised.
tested: Home, Screener filter, Feed, Squad, Profile, Lucky Guess, refresh
limitations: No orders, payments, joins or external account connections; provider and price accuracy unverified

name: Utkarsh Kushwaha
feedback: The five-question exam flow produced a personalized recovery plan and a score card that survived refresh, with a consistent playful voice. I expected the numbers to be framed as entertainment rather than reliable prediction: the output asserted 85% survival and claimed skipped topics were 80% of the exam without evidence.
tested: 38% Medium Rare result, recovery plan, scorecard, refresh retained result
limitations: Other event branches and external sharing not tested

name: Rahul Arora
feedback: Shotspace has a credible browse-to-detail journey: Delhi filtering reduced 13 spaces to four, and changing two hours to three recalculated the total from ₹3,172 to ₹4,758 and removed late slots. I expected the same completeness in the protected host/booking journey and a clearly demonstrated checkout; no booking or purchase was made.
tested: Home, Studios city filter, Velvet Sound Room detail and hours pricing
Equipment, My bookings sign-in gate, Host sign-in gate
limitations: No booking/payment; authenticated management and saved checkout state unknown

name: Harnoor Kaur Dhanjal
feedback: Logic Lab has a coherent onboarding, case library and practice structure, and the interrupted case offered a resume link even after refresh. The first coach response was only “They sell through dine-in” to a revenue-versus-cost question, while a brand-new profile was already assigned a recurring weakness; I expected complete responsive coaching and evidence-based personalization.
tested: Onboarding; all five nav screens; Dough Dilemma response advanced to stage 2
limitations: Full eight-stage case scoring not completed

name: Sudharshan Rajou
feedback: StudyBuddy explains its teach, test and read modes clearly with a clean, consistent landing page. All learning modes lead to sign-in, so I could not assess lesson generation, quiz feedback or progress; provide a sample learning session or guest access.
limitations: Authenticated features unknown; no account created or files uploaded

name: Ibadat Randhawa
feedback: The reaction game is focused and complete at its core: wait/flash/result states worked, difficulty-specific bests updated, and attempt history survived refresh. Explain what each difficulty changes so users can interpret and compare their attempts; the compact interface otherwise makes the task easy to understand.
tested: Difficulty controls and refresh retained history
limitations: Timing numbers reflect automated review latency, not human reflex performance; false-start path not confirmed

name: Revathi Iyer
feedback: CaseCrack offers a substantial structured practice experience: a custom issue-tree branch was accepted and selecting an investigation revealed relevant market data. I expected better continuity for a new learner—Beginner still opened the advanced flagship case, refresh returned to the dashboard, and seeded solved/streak metrics obscure actual progress; preserve session state and label demo history clearly.
tested: Added Competitive response pillar, revealed Market Size & Growth
Home, Practice, Company Packs, Progress, Profile; refresh
limitations: Nine-stage final score and all firm packs not exhausted

name: Maneet Kaur Tandon
feedback: Rasad presents a clear restaurant procurement dashboard with useful inventory, cost and savings priorities. The supplied Stitch preview still behaves as a first pass: Plan, Inventory, Suppliers and Orders remain on the dashboard, while Edit Plan led to an empty preview; turn these into a working review-and-save procurement loop.
limitations: Stitch prototype supplied; no purchase action attempted

name: Jahnavi Saxena
feedback: LinguaFlow delivers a useful translation result and a complete four-question quiz whose 20 XP and streak survive refresh. The communication and learning sections are coherent; make the Daily Challenge button reliably open a visible challenge, and carry the same dependable feedback through the remaining practice modes.
tested: Daily Challenge click gave no visible challenge
limitations: Microphone and speech playback not tested
Two-person conversation and AI tutoring not fully exercised

name: Kaustubh Jain
feedback: The state-aware chat, document vault and official-help directory form a thoughtful, coherent legal-information journey, and a synthetic question returned a contextual response. Finish the visible localization keys and repeated intake categories, and give each legal claim a directly inspectable source rather than a generic secondary-reference label.
tested: Synthetic Delhi consumer question answered with caution
limitations: Legal correctness not independently audited
Document generation/signing and external helplines not tested
Unrelated preloaded document records not modified

name: Kanav Sahni
feedback: The archival-photo guessing concept is distinctive, and both timer expiry and a placed map guess produced a clear year/location score and the next round. The map visibly carries an API-key-required watermark; fix that production dependency and preserve a game across refresh so the otherwise polished loop feels dependable.
limitations: Five-round completion and final leaderboard not reached
Historical-image provenance not independently verified

Tighten the scoring explanation: this run was criticised for an early stop while Timing scored 9/10, and one completed call appeared twice in recent history; these inconsistencies weaken an otherwise thoughtful learning tool.

Refresh keeps results; two duplicate records observed

Shared leaderboard backend not independently verified

name: Archit Sagar Jain

limitations: No OAuth authorization performed; all core functionality unknown

name: Shresht B S Setty
feedback: Retrofit OS has a consistent visual identity, though the dark input labels could use stronger contrast. The supplied link stops at a sign-in screen with no demo route; provide reviewer access so the sustainability workflow and outputs can be evaluated.
tested: Email/password gate and Contact Sales text
limitations: No credentials supplied; all product functionality unknown

name: Sukhman Jaggi

tested: Live URL shows No Lovable project
limitations: No app UI or functionality accessible

name: Arpit Mor
feedback: Tribe has a lively visual identity and a clear small-community proposition. The product requires account creation or sign-in before any community can be explored; include a guest route or reviewer credentials so discovery, joining and meetup flows can be assessed.
limitations: No account created; all community functionality unknown

name: Siddharth Srivastava
feedback: FormFit connects onboarding, a three-day plan, set logging and a persisted calendar streak in a clear training interface. Respect the equipment constraint: my bodyweight-only plan still included Band Row and Dumbbell Step-Up; also finish a session with a distinct summary instead of leaving the active timer and logging screen open.
tested: One synthetic set logged and session finished

Camera feature explicitly future phase; not used
Full workout and rescheduling not tested

name: Rashmika Goel
feedback: TailTime has a warm, well-composed landing page and a clear pet-care proposition. Continuing is explicitly tied to accepting terms, with no independent demo route, so provide review access that allows the vet, nutrition and stay workflows to be tested without account commitments.
tested: GetStarted/social/email routes and terms requirement inspected
limitations: Did not accept terms, authenticate, book or grant permissions; core functionality unknown

name: Siddhanth Rajpal
feedback: TradeBridge gives buyers a clear cluster-to-product discovery path; the wallet search correctly reduced five listings to one, and specifications, supplier details and RFQ context are well structured. Make registry checks and trust scores traceable to dated evidence and label seeded conversations clearly before presenting the product as independently verified sourcing.

Registry claims/ratings and actual translations unverified

name: Rahul Rawat
feedback: AllPlay Bets completes its explicitly virtual loop: selecting odds, staking 100 credits, settling a win and recording the correct 10,160 balance all worked and persisted. One outcome tested; insufficient balance and losing bet not exercised

feedback: Postcardtrails has a considered luxury-travel visual language, useful destination filters and clear experience inclusions; switching currency also changed the displayed price. Profile/authenticated screens unknown
Price conversion accuracy and availability not verified

tested: Session staticRecording03:42 and transcript without input

No coach booking

feedback: Vow is a thoughtfully structured wedding-vendor workspace, with coherent leads, quotations, payment schedules, clashes and a separate client preview. Adding a synthetic lead updated the pipeline, but refresh deleted it; make persistence reliable and clarify the conversion-rate denominator, since the headline says 83% beside 5 of 11 enquiries while the explanation uses only decided enquiries.
tested: Calendar clash and payment status inspected

No production integration or access isolation validated

Publish a directly accessible app or provide an approved review route so the actual interface and core experience can be assessed.

name: Tarushi Tyagi
feedback: Devil’s Advocate establishes an engaging boardroom premise with structured case inputs, presets and configurable adversity. The selected Kirana case stalled at the first examiner-evaluation screen across repeated checks, leaving the response box disabled, and refresh lost the session; add bounded loading, recovery and saved progress so a user can reach cross-examination and a verdict.
tested: First round remained evaluating over repeated checks across several minutes;inputdisabled

Other presets and Brutal mode not tested

name: Sahithi Paramatmuni
feedback: MurderMint has a strong atmosphere and a substantial solo deduction loop: movement, a suspect/weapon suggestion, private evidence and automatic notepad updates all worked, with a useful chronology. Final accusation/win/loss not completed
Audio settings and rejoining not tested

name: Gurjot Singh
feedback: Momentum is a focused, dependable habit tracker: creating, completing and renaming a habit kept its streak and history intact after refresh, and pre-start dates were correctly disabled. The clear empty states and honest device-local storage make the small scope feel finished; a restore/import route alongside JSON export would strengthen the backup story.
limitations: Custom schedules, deletion and JSON export/import not exercised
No cross-device sync claimed

feedback: Tagalong communicates a clear spontaneous-hangout idea with a distinctive, soft visual style. Get Started leads directly to account creation or Google sign-in, so provide a guest demo that lets reviewers assess nearby discovery, joining and safety controls without creating an account.
limitations: No account or location permission; hangout/chat functionality unknown

feedback: Ledger Insights gives a credible banking-campaign analysis view: city filters changed the measures, suppression logic is clearly explained, and stub connectors are honestly labelled. The simulated CRM push changed its row but reset on refresh, while Upload lead file opened no visible flow; complete and persist the intake-to-sync workflow, and reconcile campaign totals with the event-level figures.

No contact data uploaded or externally transmitted
CSV exports and exhaustive dataset accuracy not verified

feedback: The Last Stall turns venue choice into a well-designed learning loop, with audience fit, pricing, research credits, a forecast and a useful post-mortem; round one correctly carried its ₹30,160 gain into the next bankroll. Preserve the season across refresh and keep the revenue, margin and overhead calculation visible in the debrief so users can explain the result as well as celebrate it.
limitations: Five-round final score/DNA not reached
Other categories,timeout/bankruptcypaths not tested
